summaries.text: The article announces the availability of a podcast episode titled My AI podcast with James Pethokoukis, which includes a transcript.

The provided text contains only an error message and does not include the article body required to summarize the event. Consequently, no facts about France, the EU, or the Iris² satellite constellation can be reported.

The Hub hosts a discussion on BRICS entering a new phase of cooperation after its 20th anniversary. Experts Wang Guan, Marta Regina Fernandez, Evandro Carvalho, and Liang Yan explore the bloc's priorities and opportunities for the wider Global South as global dynamics shift.

China's pure battery electric vehicle sales rose 0.8% in August, marking the only growth among powertrain categories as all engine-powered vehicles declined. Tesla China sales fell 12.4% for a third consecutive month, yet the brand's Shanghai factory exports rose 38.7% while overall Chinese NEV exports surged 154.7% in August.

The National Medical Commission announced the approval of 13,186 new MBBS seats for the 2026-27 academic year. This decision increases the total approved undergraduate medical intake to 1,40,214 seats across 836 medical colleges, excluding Institutes of National Importance. The largest allocations among the states mentioned went to Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

OpenAI published a claimed solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems carrying a $1 million award each. The lab stated the proof was produced by an internal AI model utilizing roughly 10,000 agents rather than human mathematicians. However, rivals contested OpenAI's account of events before the proof was published.

Political editor Anand Mishra contrasts the non-controversial success of the biopic Hanuman Ansh with recent films that sparked legal and social disputes. The article notes that older religious movies like Jai Santoshi Maa achieved commercial success without creating communal divides, unlike recent productions. Mishra questions whether modern filmmakers are prioritizing political agendas and hate-mongering over art to generate box-office revenue.

Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and called on other staff to rethink their work, stating that Anthropic and OpenAI are acting irresponsibly in their pursuit of AI. Coxon, who worked at both companies over the past three years, warned on X that the firms are racing toward self-improving superintelligence that could become too powerful for humans to control and pose existential risks.

Google Trends data indicates a significant surge in Indian curiosity regarding matcha, with searches rising up to 2,500% compared to coffee. The article reports that while interest in health benefits and home preparation methods has grown, these figures reflect online curiosity rather than proven consumption habits. Seasonal flavor combinations and lifestyle products also saw breakout searches, suggesting a broader cultural engagement with the drink.

The National Weather Service issued heat advisories across California's Central Valley and coastal areas as extreme temperatures are forecast to reach 105F in Los Angeles and 100F in Sacramento. The California Independent System Operator forecasts peak power demand will hit 47,379 megawatts Wednesday, driving wholesale power prices in Southern California to $87.69 per megawatt-hour. Bloomberg reports temperatures could remain high through Thursday before sliding by mid-month.

Delhi will host the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam from September 11 to 13, prompting significant travel disruptions. The Airports Authority of India notified temporary airspace restrictions for non-scheduled flights within a 300-km radius of New Delhi, people familiar with the matter said according to HT reports. Meanwhile, Northern Railway announced cancellations, diversions, and rescheduling of several train services due to operational requirements linked to the summit.

An Archaeological Survey of India officer inspected a 20-foot deep structure found beneath a demolished mosque in Saharanpur. ASI Assistant Archaeological Officer Manoj Kumar Yadav noted the construction resembles a medieval well but emphasized that its age and origin require evidence. He cautioned against linking the site to the Shahjahan era or specific religious functions without archaeological proof such as coins or seals. Further excavation decisions await government approval.

P. Vasudevan, Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India, stated that the central bank is exploring gold tokenisation to overcome challenges in current modes. Vasudevan noted that tokenisation could fulfill these needs while maintaining interoperability in the payments ecosystem. The RBI has already experimented with tokenised financial-market instruments through the Unified Markets Interface and piloted tokenised certificates of deposit, with plans to add more asset classes to expand the ecosystem.

Anthropic announced Thursday that it disrupted several state-sponsored surveillance operations using its artificial intelligence models between January and July. The company stated these campaigns originated in China, Iran, and West Africa, targeting groups including Hong Kong pro-democracy activists. Additionally, Anthropic alleged that Chinese developers Moonshot and Deepseek secretly used its Claude model to generate user responses and train their own systems. The report noted that some of this data potentially violated privacy agreements.

Inox Wind Limited clarified to the BSE and NSE on September 7, 2026, that a 100 MW turnkey order was received from Terra Clean Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation Limited, rather than directly from IOCL. The company stated the previous announcement incorrectly identified IOCL as the direct customer due to an inadvertent error in the press release framing. Deepak Banga, Company Secretary, digitally signed the correction issued to the stock exchanges.

The NSE Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex declined on Wednesday, with the Nifty 50 closing at 23,431.50 and the Sensex at 74,764.23. The Nifty IT index led sector losses, dropping more than 3%, while the Nifty Metal index gained around 2%. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, stated that the 23,400 zone serves as immediate support, though momentum indicators indicate significant market weakness. Kumar Gaurav, the article's author, clarified he is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst.

President Donald Trump escalated his trade dispute with Canada by issuing executive orders to ban alcohol imports and impose a 50% tariff on specific goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney acknowledged the economic cost of loosening ties but insisted the benefits would outweigh the pain. Canada has already implemented retaliatory tariffs on US imports, while Trump threatened to bar Canadian companies from US government contracts. The two nations have not resumed negotiations since talks broke down in August.

President Donald Trump suggested renaming New Mexico to New America, a proposal quickly rejected by Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham. AFP reported that this suggestion follows a pattern of Trump's second-term naming moves, including the formal renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America. While some media reports suggest the New Mexico proposal may have originated as an internet hoax, the Lake Ontario change remains an official executive order. The state's governor noted the name has existed since before the United States.

The Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) released a briefing note stating that solar sharer tariffs, which provide free daytime electricity, could save Australian households thousands of dollars annually when paired with consumption shifts. IEEFA modelling indicates savings of up to $2,257 per year for households with two electric vehicles, while also highlighting barriers such as limited appliance flexibility and regulatory hurdles for renters. The organisation recommends policy measures to extend free electricity windows and improve feed-in tariffs to maximise benefits.

US inflation remained unchanged at 3. 4% in August, with gasoline prices rising 3. 9% and pushing the overall rate above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Diesel prices hit a new high above $6 per gallon, fueled by global oil price spikes linked to US-Iran conflict escalations. Consequently, 85% of traders now expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point next week to slow price increases, despite Chair Kevin Warsh remaining tight-lipped on specific decisions.

Vietnam is preparing to transition its power system toward virtual power plants by aggregating distributed rooftop solar, battery storage, and electric vehicles. According to a publication by the Ministry of Industry and Trade, authorities are exploring aggregation platforms to link these resources into flexible grid assets. The ministry noted that while the country has overbuilt solar, creating grid bottlenecks, VPP aggregation could offer benefits. However, the ministry stated that a suitable roadmap and mechanism are needed so dispersed resources can participate in the electricity market effectively and transparently.

The White House is considering using the Defense Production Act to expand U. S. refining capacity, according to Reuters. American refineries are currently operating at 98% capacity, prompting discussions during a meeting between President Donald Trump and refiners. Executives indicated that federal funds would accelerate expansion of existing plants compared to building new facilities. The Defense Production Act allows the president to provide financial assistance for materials and capacity deemed necessary for national defense. This follows a presidential determination in April declaring domestic petroleum production essential to national defense. U. S.

The Kerala government has shortlisted three revenue land sites in Ernakulam for the proposed J.C. Daniel International Film City, announced under the Revised State Budget for 2026-27. Culture Minister P. Vishnunadh stated that work is expected to commence within six months to address the lack of adequate studio infrastructure in Malayalam cinema. The project, planned under a public-private partnership model, will include sprawling studio floors, an entertainment zone, and an exhibition centre. Industry representatives, including B. Rakesh of the Kerala Film Producers' Association, noted that subsidized rates for facilities could reduce movie budgets.

Anthropic announced Thursday that it blocked attempts by malicious actors to utilize its artificial intelligence for cyberattacks, surveillance, and biological weapon development. The company detailed findings from its third misuse report since March 2025, which included a blocked request for Claude to assist in a grant application for gain-of-function research on the chikungunya virus. Anthropic noted that while older models were less capable of aiding sophisticated biological research, newer models pose greater risks, prompting the implementation of stricter safeguards. The report follows concerns raised by a resigning researcher regarding the industry's rapid development of powerful AI systems.

Germany requested the International Court of Justice to dismiss a legal challenge filed by Nicaragua regarding arms exports to Israel. Nicaragua accuses Berlin of aiding genocide in Gaza, whereas Germany argues the case lacks jurisdiction and proper procedural steps were not followed. The German government noted that its weapons export policies remain strictly regulated. While an initial bid for an emergency injunction failed in 2024, Germany suspended exports briefly in 2025 before resuming them following a truce. A decision on dismissing the case is tentatively expected later this year, potentially contingent on separate proceedings concerning Israel's actions in Gaza.

Amy Winecoff reports that New York's Stop Addictive Feeds Exploitation (SAFE) for Kids Act provides an early model for age assurance governance. The final rules, released on July 28, require ongoing evaluation of systems against criteria balancing efficacy, privacy, and availability. However, the article notes significant gaps, including a lack of accuracy standards for false rejections and insufficient public transparency regarding certification reports. Winecoff argues that future regulations should mandate multiple age assurance options and establish comprehensive end-to-end performance standards. Additionally, the author suggests that making certification data public would allow independent researchers to better evaluate system performance and inform future policy updates.

Apple CEO John Ternus unveiled the company's latest products, including the foldable iPhone Duo and the iPhone 18 series, at an event in Cupertino. The Duo, priced at $1,999, features a 7.6-inch display and will be available in October, marking Apple's entry into the foldable smartphone category. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models will launch in September with enhanced battery life and camera capabilities. Analysts suggest that while the Duo is a significant design addition, foldable phones remain a niche market. Ternus emphasized Apple's focus on privacy and security in its new AI features, distinguishing the company from rivals like Samsung and Google.

IBM and Lockheed Martin, together with ETH Zurich, have launched a new quantum innovation hub in Switzerland. This initiative will be anchored by the country's first IBM Quantum System Two, which is expected to be operational at the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre in Lugano by the end of 2026. ETH Zurich will coordinate access and provide expertise, while IBM will operate the system. The hub aims to expand quantum computing access for Swiss academia, startups, and industry to advance research in areas such as chemistry and materials science. Additionally, the project extends the strategic collaboration between IBM and Lockheed Martin, combining their respective innovations in quantum computing and sensing.

W Health Ventures, a Mumbai-based healthcare venture capital firm, announced the closure of its second fund at 700 crore, surpassing the initial target of 630 crore. The firm plans to utilize this capital to build eight to 10 healthcare companies from the pre-idea stage over the next four years. Managing partner Dr Pankaj Jethwani explained that the company creation model identifies gaps in healthcare delivery and recruits founding teams to address structural mismatches. Unlike conventional funds, W Health Ventures develops businesses from the idea stage, having already launched two companies under Fund II that have reached 25 million patients. The firm intends to expand this approach across India and the US-India corridor.

Samsung India has reportedly initiated layoffs affecting 80-100 executives within its television and home appliance divisions, according to the Economic Times. The company cites rising input costs, weaker sales, and margin pressure as primary drivers for these cuts, which include director-level officials and branch managers. While the electronics business faces challenges, the smartphone division remains spared as it constitutes the majority of revenue. Additionally, Samsung is consolidating its branch network by merging offices in cities like Ranchi with Patna and Delhi with Gurgaon. The Economic Times noted that termination letters are being issued in small batches without notice periods, with affected employees receiving severance equivalent to three months' salary plus additional pay for years of service.

The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) published a survey of nearly 19,500 people across 15 European countries indicating that while public support for higher defense spending is growing, it remains conditional on economic stability. Jana Kobzova, co-director of ECFR's European Security Programme, told Anadolu that voters understand the changing security landscape but insist governments prioritize the economic squeeze. The poll found that only 39% of respondents supported reducing public spending to fund defense, while 45% opposed such trade-offs. Support for this approach varied sharply by country, ranging from 55% in Estonia to just 28% in Austria. The findings suggest that Europeans are more receptive to defense investment when it strengthens European industrial capacity rather than relying on external suppliers.

The Sydney Philharmonia Choirs recently returned from a 12-day tour of the UK, where amateur singers performed at the Royal Albert Hall as part of the BBC Proms. According to choir members like Kate Clowes and Joel Wilkinson, the group largely consists of people with day jobs who self-fund their participation and travel. Artistic Director Brett Weymark noted that during the tour, these individuals temporarily become professional musicians dedicated solely to singing. The performance, which featured over 300 performers, was broadcast on ABC Classic. Weymark compares community music groups to local sports teams, emphasizing their vital role in grassroots music making. Members reported that the experience provided significant professional development and strengthened friendships, creating a unique sense of connection through shared musical joy.

Apple Inc shares dropped 1.3% to $315 on September 8 ahead of an event where the company plans to unveil its first foldable iPhone. Analysts anticipate the device, expected to cost more than $2,500, could quickly become a category leader despite potential limitations in camera and processor technology. Nabila Popal of IDC stated that the phone would sell well due to Apple's ability to create an aura of exclusivity. The introduction also marks a debut for CEO John Ternus, who took the role on September 1. Apple aims to refresh its Pro models while delaying updates to other lines until spring 2027. This move represents a significant design shift in the iPhone's nearly 20-year history, following years of internal research initiated by then-CEO Tim Cook around 2020.

In September 2026, NVIDIA announced it is leaning into native GPU programming in Rust, aiming to mature CUDA Rust through 2027 and beyond. The company addresses the gap where GPU kernels previously required separate languages by enabling Rust code to compile natively to PTX. NVIDIA presents two tracks matching CUDA's existing models: SIMT for thread-level control and Tile for compiler-managed data tiles. The Tile track is recommended first for its architecture-agnostic design. Two projects demonstrate these capabilities: cuda-oxide, an early alpha codegen backend requiring a nightly toolchain, and cutile-rs, a published crate supporting stable Rust. Both projects enforce memory safety by preventing data races at compile time, though they differ in their approach to ownership and shared memory. NVIDIA notes that both projects are early-stage and not yet production-ready, inviting community feedback and collaboration.

The European Central Bank raised interest rates to 2.5% on Thursday, citing heightened inflation risks linked to renewed conflict in the Middle East. The central bank increased rates from 2.25% and adjusted its economic growth forecast for the eurozone. ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that headline inflation is expected to return to target by the end of 2027, supported by higher interest rates. Simultaneously, energy prices jumped after US and Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, causing Brent crude to pass $105 a barrel. These spikes drove government borrowing costs to historic highs in the UK, Germany, and France. Analysts at Schroders noted that while core inflation remains stable, higher energy prices will likely keep headline inflation elevated. Concerns persist over low EU gas storage levels ahead of winter, which could further strain inflation if supplies are disrupted.

Shares of Tata Motors Ltd traded largely flat on Monday as its voluntary tender offer for Iveco Group formally entered the acceptance phase. As of 11.19 am, the stock was quoted at ₹458.50. Tata Motors, through its subsidiary TML CV Holdings B.V., launched a recommended all-cash voluntary tender offer for all common shares of Iveco Group N.V. The acceptance period runs from September 7, 2026, through October 26, 2026. The offer price is €14.10 per common share, cum dividend, valuing Iveco Group at approximately €3.82 billion. The Iveco board has unanimously recommended the offer to its shareholders. Exor N.V., Iveco's largest shareholder with around 27.06 percent of common shares, has irrevocably committed to tender its stake. All required regulatory clearances have been obtained. The offer requires a minimum acceptance threshold of 95 percent of common shares, which reduces to 80 percent if shareholders approve the Back-End Resolution at the extraordinary general meeting scheduled for October 16, 2026.
